<>Planar Polish <><><>Tool: FT Sponge , Palm sander <>Abrasive: Med scotchbrite/ Foamtec <>Finish: Random brush <> <><><>Manual polish of the wet part after the DI Water is required to physically remove any incoming surface deposits before acid bath treatment. Use the maroon (medium) scotch brite scrub as required at the edges of all parts to remove the deposits at the edge ONLY. Use on the flat regions of the part only if presence of thick deposits are observed. The manual polish of the flat regions is done using a two-step method: 800 grit followed by 1350 grit Foamtec Pads. This two-step process is required to remove any visible color variation or other non-conformities. The incoming dents or scratches during part handling will not be removed by the planar polish step and should be documented before the start of planar polish. During the planar polish process, DI Water should be used frequently to remove the polish debris. Also, the polish pads should be supported by polish sponge on the flat regions, and the polishing done in an orbital pattern.

<>Final Inspection <><><>Ensure no scratches or contaminant are visible. Utilize a LED flashlight to inspect inside the valve body, ensure no residual contamination is present. Also use an IPA wipe inside the valve body to detect any residuals. If any stains, scratches, or any visual residual is present, inform process engineer or production supervisor for determination of re-processing requirements or issuance to NC product. Any final discrepancies need to be documented on the IMR W/O and MSR-FSR W/O (documentation needs to detail the exact location of the damage or disrepancy, eg. scratch on body''s lower right inner wall, scratches on flange sear surface, etc.)

<>Incoming Inspection <><><>Verify that the Intel Hitachi chamber stainless steel run card is included inside of the lid of the transit case. Inspect the run card to confirm that the Intel verification section has been signed off by outgoing Intel technicians. Using ESCA/QA, print of a work order for the relevent kit to be refurbished. Also print of a copy of the work order label and place on the transit case the kit was received in. The completed kit must be shipped back in the same transit case. Check all parts for knicks, scratches, and bends to the edges and O-ring sealing surfaces. If any nonconformities are found regarding the run card or with the parts, contact the Production Manager. The procedure for any non conformities found is to use a "yellow tag" process. Once a non conformity is found, note details of this onto the hard copy of the work order, entering as much details as possible such as part name, damage type such a scratch or dent, location of the damage on the part etc. Also state that the part is to be labelled with a "yellow tag" at final inspection. A tracking sheet should be set up to document and capture all "yellow tag" non conformities found. All nonconformities need to be relayed to the tool/part owner for disposition. Once disposition is obtained, the tracking sheet should be populated with this information. This tracking sheet can then be referenced each time the kit/parts are sent of refurbishment and that the same parts does not need to be "yellow tagged" each time its received and inspected. Check shipping case for damage inlcuding castors, latches, hinges or other damage. Report any damage found to Production Manager. All parts within a kit shall be processed as a batch and not mixed with another kit.
